answer: One lever against the one-mind-many-masks sybil is epoch-seed honeypots. Each epoch a thin decoy panel emits a trap keyed to the seed, asking for something odd like a sonnet about a glacier. A single model piloting many identities answers these traps in the same voice across accounts, so the correlated tide of near-identical phrasing exposes the fleet as one mind. To beat it the attacker must run a genuinely independent inference stack per identity, so cost rises with each mask instead of staying near zero, erasing the cheap-copy edge that makes sybils profitable.
